newsitem.title: UK: Dlr/mark firm in Europe but backs off fresh highs.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/mark firm in Europe but backs off fresh highs.

text.p: The dollar made a firm start in early Europe against the mark and yen, testing a fresh six-year high just above 1.84 marks before backtracking slightly.
Dealers said the apparent tolerance by the Bundesbank of current mark levels and the lack of overt mark support from Thursday's council meeting continued to provide dollar support.

Dollar/Swiss franc was also higher, climbing above 1.51 to reach its highest levels since August 1993. Dealers said the move was mainly technical, boosted by Thursday's dollar gains above key resistance in the 1.4900-30 francs area and options-related hedging above the 1.50 level.

The press statement after Thursday's Bundesbank council meeting, its last before the four-week summer recess, said the central bank was paying attention to developments in the mark and financial markets.

"This was pretty bland so it was not hard to take dollar/mark higher," said a U.S. bank dealer. "But we've had more Buba comments since then which are giving people something to chew on into the weekend."
Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing said late Thursday that he could not say he was unconcerned about the speed and size of the dollar's gains against the mark.

Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen said in Friday's Handelsblatt newspaper the decision to fix the repo for only two weeks over the four-week summer break showed the central bank was 'driving carefully' in the current environment.

"This gives a strong signal that if the mark weakens further, the Bundesbank will have the freedom to respond," said Nick Parsons, currency strategist at Paribas. "It shows that not all the Bundesbank is out on holiday."
Dealers said the market has taken some of this on board but expectations remain low that the Bundesbank will respond to mark weakness with monetary policy changes.
By 0830 GMT, dollar/mark stood at 1.8362/67 after touching a fresh six-year high earlier of 1.8403. It stood at 1.8310/20 late Thursday in Europe.

Dollar/Swiss franc was also off its earlier peak of 1.5175 but still seen firm, trading at 1.5116/26 in morning Europe against 1.5020/30 on Thursday. The mark was slightly firmer on its European crosses and managed to recover some of its recent losses against the Swiss franc.
The most important U.S. data due today are June durable goods orders, where a 1.4 percent rise is forecast after a 0.6 percent drop in May.
Dollar/yen eased back from its earlier, nearly one-month highs but was still holding above 116 in morning trade.

Overnight comments from Japan's Economic Planning Agency that its overall economic view did not differ from the Bank of Japan's, which analysts said implied a modest, slowing recovery, eroded some yen support.
"The fixed income market in Japan is pretty relaxed about interest rates and there is a lack of short-term rate support for the yen," said Eric Fishwick, economist at Nikko Europe.
Dollar/yen was trading at 116.15/20 against 115.87/92 late on Thursday. -- Andrew Reierson, London forex +44 171 542 6745
